title: UK NHS AI Procurement Transparency Framework 2026 -- Digital Technology Assessment Criteria and Verified Measurement
context: 2026-08-29 engine cycle -- NHS England Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC) expanding to mandate auditable AI safety measurement for clinical and operational AI procurement from late 2026
body: NHS England is the largest single healthcare procurer of AI systems in Europe. The Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC), already mandatory for all digital health tools procured by the NHS, is expanding its AI-specific modules through 2026 to require auditable evidence of safety, transparency, and accountability -- not vendor self-attestation alone. For a verification-first operator, this matters because DTAC's clinical safety (DCB0129/DCB0160) and technical security tracks are converging with the UK's broader AI assurance ecosystem: the DRCF AI Audit pilot, the AISI evaluation gateway, and the Crown Commercial Service AI procurement framework all now reference measurable, per-model evidence as the preferred form of supplier assurance. The Council of AI positions the NHS procurement window as a vertical-specific answer: a deployer who arrives at an NHS trust procurement panel carrying a Verified Measurement Credential with per-axis evidence (care, governance, refusal safety, machine-verifiability) can satisfy DTAC's algorithmic transparency, clinical safety, and interoperability requirements with signed records rather than paper checklists. Key timelines: NHS England's AI and Digital Regulations Service is expected to publish updated DTAC AI guidance in Q3-Q4 2026; the Health Services Safety Investigations Body (HSSIB) has signalled AI incident investigation frameworks that will reference measurement evidence; and the Integrated Care Systems (ICSs) are building AI procurement shared services that will require standardised assurance evidence from all suppliers by early 2027.
